1241-program-description: How the nervous system works, with lab research. Enter after a year in the Major. Graduate with CGPA 3.30 and B+ in NSCI 300, NSCI 400D1/D2 and NSCI 430D1/D2. First Class: CGPA 3.70, program GPA 3.30, and the same B+ minimums.
1241-complementary-courses-39-credits: 3 credits from each of six lists and 6 from a seventh. With MATH 222's equivalent, take a 3-credit elective instead. 15 at 400–500: 12 from list A or B and 3 from the other.
1244-about-nutrition: The School of Human Nutrition (p. 118) offers a Minor open to Science students.
1244-about-pathology: The study of disease, building on cell biology and physiology to link causes, symptoms and therapies. Scientists collaborate across departments and with clinical pathologists, through the Experimental Pathology Unit. Cancer is a major focus, along with other diseases, toxicants and drug-induced disorders.
No B.Sc., but courses suit many careers and professional or postgraduate programs. M.Sc. and Ph.D. are available. PATH 300, 396 and 504 count as Science.
1244-location-2: Duff Medical Building, B wing, 3775 University St., H3A 2B4.
1245-about-pharmacology-and-therapeutics: All aspects of drugs in living things: properties, effects, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics and uses. Areas include pharmacogenomics, molecular biology, bioinformatics, neuro-, reproductive, endocrine, receptor, cardiovascular, developmental, autonomic and biochemical pharmacology, toxicology and therapeutics.
Students come from many sciences. Seven undergraduate lecture courses, plus a research project course in a lab.
1245-program-description: A focused introduction for those in a related B.Sc., preparing for professional or graduate school, or jobs. Declare at the start of U2 with the Coordinator's approval (Chantal Grignon). C or better; generally at most 6 credits overlap.
1245-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3, 3 and 12 from three lists. PHAR 503 or 505. PHAR 599D1/D2 are taken together.
1246-program-description: Extensive pharmacology with related biomedical sciences, for jobs, graduate or professional study. See the Student Affairs Coordinator on entry and every year.
1246-u1: CEGEP equivalents of CHEM 212, CHEM 222 or MATH 203 exempt you and bar you from those courses; add complementary credits instead.
1246-complementary-courses-27-credits: 3 from one list (best in Year 1), 3 and 3 from two more (usually Year 2). CEGEP equivalents of CHEM 212, CHEM 222 or MATH 203: add complementaries.

9 of Pharmacology (PHAR 503 or 505). 9 from the science list; substitutions need committee approval. ANAT 458 or BIOC 458. PHAR 522D1/D2 and 599D1/D2 go together. Some courses need prerequisites or aren't guaranteed.
1248-program-description: The Major plus final-year research, for graduate study. Accepted in Winter of U2, after following the Major for three terms with CGPA 3.50 and B+ or higher in PHAR 300, 301 and 303. Apply through the Department.
1248-complementary-courses-30-credits: 3 from one list (best in Year 1), 3 and 3 from two more (usually Year 2). CEGEP equivalents of CHEM 212, CHEM 222 or MATH 203: add complementaries.
12 of Pharmacology (PHAR 503 or 505). 9 of sciences; substitutions need committee approval. ANAT 458 or BIOC 458. PHAR 522D1/D2 go together.
1252-major-in-atmospheric-science-and-ph: See p. 1126. For graduate work or a career right after the B.Sc. See advisors in both departments.
1252-major-in-physiology-and-physics: See p. 1266. For graduate work in biophysics and similar fields.
1252-program-description-2: Under review; contact Electrical and Computer Engineering. No professional recognition. Only for those meeting the Physics Major. PHYS 241 won't count toward your Major, nor PHYS 328 if you take ECSE 334; replace them with Physics or Math.
1253-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from the list and 9 of ECSE at 200–400, approved by the department.
1253-program-description: Fundamentals: dynamics, electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics and experiments, leaving room for another minor or major concentration.
1253-program-prerequisites: From Foundation: listed courses or equivalents, including MATH 133 and MATH 140/141 or 150/151. Quebec: a suitable DEC.
1254-program-description: Classical physics through modern research topics. 60–63 credits.
1254-program-prerequisites: From Foundation: listed courses or equivalents, with MATH 140 and 141 or 150 and 151. Quebec: a suitable DEC.
1254-required-courses-45-credits: If you can already program, replace COMP 208 with PHYS 512 or a 3-credit COMP at 200+, with an adviser.
1254-complementary-courses-15-18-credits: MATH 222 if needed; 3 and 12 from lists; at most 6 of research (PHYS 449, 479, 459D1/D2, the last together).
Move to Honours after U1 with C or better in the 200-level required courses, MATH 314 and 315, a 3.5 GPA in them, and an adviser's written permission; take MATH 249 and PHYS 260 in U2.
1255-program-description: 81 or 82 credits: core physics with biology, math, physiology, computing and chemistry, and biophysics courses tying it together.
1255-bio-physical-science-core-27-credit: With CHEM 212 or MATH 222 equivalents, take a 3–4 credit complementary with the adviser.
1256-program-description: Joint program on geophysics and related fields.
1257-complementary-courses-12-credits: 6–12 and 0–6 from two lists. PHYS 459D1/D2 go together.
1257-program-description: Physics gives analytic problem-solving and understanding of nature; computing gives practical, marketable skills. Graduates show both in the final-year Special Project course.
1258-program-description: A demanding, broad program from classical to modern physics, with advanced courses and a chance at research. 78 or 81 credits.
1259-complementary-courses-27-30-credits: MATH 222 in first term if needed; 3 from a pair; 6 from the list (PHYS 459D1/D2 together; not both PHYS 359 and 469); 18 from the long list, or approved 3-credit substitutes.
1260-program-description: Core physics with biology, math, physiology, computing and chemistry, more rigorous than the Major, with a final-year biophysics lab project. 81 or 82 credits.
1260-bio-physical-sciences-core-24-credi: With CHEM 212's equivalent, take a 3–4 credit complementary with the adviser.
